  0      Something’s come up about the conference in Munich. Really important. We have to
         make a decision. Get back to me.

  1      I thought I told you the report was needed by lunchtime today. I don’t see it on my desk. I hope
         you haven’t lost it.

  2      Tony told me you talked to Sandra this morning and explained the situation. I hope it wasn’t too
         upsetting. Anyway, let me know how she took it.

         something else to surprise her.

         he blew up like a volcano. But relax. He’ll forget about it in a few days.

         start working faster, he’ll be in trouble.

Task 3
       Questions 11-15

       Read the text below.
       For each question (11-15), choose the correct answer (A, B, or C).
       Mark your answer on the answer sheet.


                                       The smartest dog in the world

     Many owners struggle to teach their dogs to sit or fetch, but John Pilley, a retired professor,
  taught his dog Chaser to understand more than 1,000 words. Chaser is an average-sized border
  collie with round eyes, mostly the colour of cookies-and-cream ice cream, but with a black patch
  right above her left eye.
     Pilley studied dogs working on sheep farms and one night around the fire he told one farmer,
  “You know science says that your dogs don’t really know their name?” The farmer responded:
  “Really? Then tell me why, when I call out my dog Jeb or Fuzz out of four dogs and ask them to go
  get Molly and Tolly, two sheep out of a hundred, they do it every time?” John Pilley realized he was
  wrong.
     Other scientists worked with monkeys showing how fast they learn through play. For Pilley, our
  connection with dogs was more special. He was sure that working one-on-one rather than with
  groups of animals must bring even better results. He believed it would be meaningful to work with
  one dog, and that was Chaser.
     Chaser was a two-month-old puppy when he started teaching her words. The first was for a blue
  ball. He named it Blue, put it in front of Chaser and said, “Catch Blue”. Then he threw it to her. On
  the third day, when she could bring him the ball from another room, he moved to another object. At
  the end of the third month of her training, only five-months-old Chaser knew 40 words.
     For three years, Mr Pilley trained Chaser for four to five hours every day. He showed her an
  object, said its name up to 40 times, then hid it and asked her to find it. She learned to recognize
  the names of 800 stuffed animals, 116 balls, 26 frisbees and a mishmash of plastic toys. Each of the
  1,022 objects Chaser knows has an individual name like “Bamboozel” or “Flipflopper.”



 11      What do we find out about Chaser from the first paragraph?

         A She is black around the right eye.
         B She likes cookies and ice cream.
         C She belongs to a former teacher.

      A They learn best when people play with them.
      B They learn best when they are in a group.
      C They learn best when they are alone.



 14   How long did it take Chaser to learn 40 words?

      A Two months.
      B Three months.
      C Five months.



 15   How did Pilley succeed in training Chaser?

      A He trained her several hours a day for three years.
      B He showed her 40 objects a day for three years.
